newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares up at noon on selective buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares up at noon on selective buying.

text.p: The Shanghai B share index was up at midday on Monday with overseas investors cautiously buying blue-chips while domestic investors were largely sidelined awaiting the remaining 1996 results, brokers said.
The B index put on 0.509 points or 0.69 percent to 73.829 points on volume of 5.99 million shares worth $3.71 million, compared with $2.3 million on Friday.

The index was pushed up by careful position-building by overseas investors in stocks which have reported good 1996 results, brokers said. But most domestic investors were sidelined with the bulk of firms yet to report for last year.

"Strong performance by Chinese shares listed abroad was perhaps the key reason triggering interest amongst overseas investors in buying some good B shares," one broker said. "But most investors are sidelined pending more company results."
Of 43 B share firms, less than 10 have so far published 1996 results with the April 30 deadline approaching.
If the blue-chips continue strongly, follow-up buying will emerge, brokers said.
Of 43 B shares, 37 traded, with 18 up, six flat and 13 down.
Shanghai Dazhong Taxi, the most actively traded counter, was the star after consolidation over the past few sessions, jumping $0.100 or 9.14 percent to $1.194 on volume of 817,800 shares.
Huangshan Tourism Development followed, up $0.036 or 6.22 percent to $0.614 on volume of 207,500 shares.
The Shanghai A share index was sharply up in active trading with fresh capital flowing into the market, brokers said.
The A share index surged 43.061 points or 3.21 percent to 1,383.654 points on volume of 664.0 million shares worth 7.7 billion yuan.
The SSE30 index gained 86.118 points or 2.45 percent to 3,598.716 points.
Jilin Province Jifa Agricultural Group was the star on speculative buying, up 1.68 yuan or 10.02 percent to 18.43 yuan on volume of 4.6 million shares.
